title: 10 Tips For Customer Support On Twitter: Part 1
description: I have personally helped Verizon Wireless launch @VZWSupport, I launched @IntelSupport into a global operation, and recently trained the new Go90 support team for their new Twitter account @Go90_helps. I’ve been on both sides of the twitter account as a social media manager and a customer.  It’s not a secret that Twitter is a fantastic customer service tool. It’s easy for customers to use and it’s also easy for companies to respond to customers. Twitter is almost as easy as texting. Now customers can send unlimited direct messages to companies via Twitter making it very easy for them to explain their situation to the agent. Companies such as Starwood Hotels are using Twitter as a way to improve customer experiences. For example, if a customer has a terrible experience with your brand and they tweet about it. Not only do you have the opportunity to fix the customer issue, but your agent can also go above and beyond to do something extra for the customer. That with said, most customers aren’t seeking anything special—they just want their problem solved. Consider this T-Mobile stat--90 percent of customers that use T-Mobile Twitter support claim they don’t need to call the call center because their issue was solved through Twitter. Twitter is good for corporate budgets. The cost of a call for a company can start at 20 dollars. Multiply that by hundreds of thousands or even millions of calls, and that’s a lot of dough! Not only do customers love the simplicity of Twitter, but it’s cost effective for companies too.  With all that said I have five tips for you around how to do Twitter customer support well. It takes time, consistency and practice. It might seem daunting at first but over time your company will learn to love Twitter customer support.  Here is the first half of my ten tips for Twitter Customer Support.
